# Metis: Independent Front-end Stack Review

**Review date:** 03/10/2026  
**Scope:** `metis-frontend-stack-pack.zip` + verification of the current state of the front-end ecosystem  
**Conclusion:** **Can be settled with conditions**

> Evidence convention: `WBS-xx`, `BLD-xx`, `PLT-xx`, `BR-xx`, `section x.y` are evidence from the BRD. `SG-5.1`, `SG-6`, `SG-7a`, `SG-9` are sections of `brand/style-guide.md`. `WF-26`, `WF-58`... are the corresponding wireframes. Sources that start with `IND-` are industry knowledge verified on 03/10/2026 and listed in the Appendix.

---

# 1. Executive summary

## 1.1 Conclusion

**Can be settled with conditions.** React + TypeScript + Vite + pnpm/Nx is a suitable foundation for Metis. React is not only a safe choice; for the three hardest interaction layers of the product, an editable `treegrid`, a node/edge canvas and a keyboard-accessible board, it has a practical advantage in ecosystem, accessibility libraries and the ability to hire/rotate people in a team of 40. [Observation: section 18.3, WBS-04..WBS-20, BLD-13, PLN-05, SG-7a] [Industry knowledge: IND-REACT-2026, IND-RAC-2026, IND-XYFLOW-2026, IND-TANSTACK-TABLE9]

However, the current technology set **should not yet be locked as it stands in order to start feature code**. The two most dangerous points are the self-built WBS table and the use of Tailwind as a direct styling language for all complex markup. TanStack Table + TanStack Virtual can be the base for the WBS, but TanStack provides only state/model and virtualization mechanics; all of the semantics, keyboard model, focus model, inline editing, sticky behavior, conflict UI and most of the accessibility contract are still owned by the Metis team. [Observation: WBS-04..WBS-06, WBS-18..WBS-20, PLT-05, PLT-06, SG-7a, WF-26] [Industry knowledge: IND-TANSTACK-TABLE9]

Tailwind should be **kept**, but not under the model of “translating all of `wireframe.css` into utility strings at the call site”. That approach loses the trace from the style guide to the code, creates very noisy markup in the grid/canvas and raises the likelihood that 40 people produce many near-identical variants. The right way is to use Tailwind as the styling engine underneath a semantic design system: CSS tokens remain the source of truth; components have stable names; complex geometry is allowed to use local CSS Modules/CSS layers; every component has a contract ID, a Storybook story and a test. [Observation: SG-6, SG-7a, `wireframe.css`, `tokens.css`] [Industry knowledge: IND-TAILWIND-THEME, IND-TAILWIND-SHADOW]

The decision to rule out AG Grid Enterprise **should be reopened as a conditional decision**, not reversed outright. AG Grid has built-in tree data, editing, column pinning, keyboard navigation and ARIA `treegrid`, but AG Grid's own accessibility documentation says virtualization can cause problems for screen readers and recommends turning virtualization off or using pagination to ensure all elements are present in the DOM. Because Metis requires a WBS of up to 2.000 items, scrolling, pinned columns and its own keyboard semantics, AG Grid is not “buy it and you are done”. An acceptance spike using exactly the WBS data and exactly SG-7a is needed before choosing. [Observation: WBS-20, section 17.1, SG-7a] [Industry knowledge: IND-AGGRID-A11Y, IND-AGGRID-KEYBOARD, IND-AGGRID-PRICE]

## 1.2 The five biggest problems

| # | Problem | Why it is big | Evidence | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The editable virtualized `treegrid` is the highest-risk item | Combines hierarchy, inline edit, bulk edit, pinned columns, saved views, conflict handling, 2.000 rows and SR/keyboard | WBS-04..06, WBS-18..20, PLT-05/06, SG-7a, section 17.1, WF-26 | Acceptance spike TanStack vs AG Grid before production feature code |
| 2 | Tailwind risks breaking the traceability of the design system | `wireframe.css` is currently a semantic map almost 1:1 with SG-6; utility-only loses the components' domain names | SG-6, SG-7a, `wireframe.css` 343 lines, `tokens.css` | Semantic component layer + `component-contracts.yaml`; Tailwind sits under that layer |
| 3 | The parity matrix does not exist yet but the canvas/list depend on it | If the editor is coded first, the two UIs will form two sets of behavior that are hard to merge | BLD-13, BR-41, section 18.4, WF-58 | Settle the command vocabulary + parity matrix before the editor implementation |
| 4 | OpenAPI is being given the role of “only source” too early | The backend is not settled; if UI types/hooks spread into the domain, Discovery will be locked in by a contract the FE imagined | section 18.4, PLT-06 | Separate the domain commands from the OpenAPI transport; call the current OpenAPI a provisional contract |
| 5 | The test strategy has one gate that is wrong in nature | A pixel diff against 58 mid-fidelity wireframes will create false positives when the app moves to high-fidelity | 58 PNG, SG-6, appendix B.3 | Wireframe conformance via structure/component contract; the visual baseline is taken from the approved app |

## 1.3 Three decisions to settle before writing production code

1. **FS-01: Grid strategy and acceptance gate.** Choose custom TanStack or AG Grid Enterprise after a Discovery spike using exactly `26-wbs-table`, data of 2.000 items, pinned code/name, inline edit, hierarchy filtering and a real screen reader. Do not decide by a feature checklist.
2. **FS-03: Styling/traceability architecture.** Settle Tailwind + a semantic design-system layer + a contract registry. Do not let the feature team write UI directly from utility classes and bypass the component contract.
3. **FS-05/06: Editor operation contract.** Settle the parity matrix schema and the canonical command API for canvas/list/keyboard/server command before writing `29-deliverable-builder` or `58-process-framework-editor`.

Three decisions can be left for later: the specific icon set, the dark mode visual design, and the time to move from `date-fns` to Temporal. The condition is that from the start the tokens must be semantic, `Icon` must have a stable abstraction, and date/time must go through one boundary module instead of importing `date-fns` scattered across the app. [Observation: SG-9]

# 2. Scoring table against the nine criteria: S1

Scale: **1 poor, 5 very good**. The scores are for **the option as currently proposed**, before applying the fix conditions in the later parts.

| Layer | Stable | Few bugs | Community | Easy to maintain | Explicit | Easy to scale | Scales fast | 5-year lifecycle | Phone → desktop |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Foundation: React + TS strict + Vite + PWA | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 |
| Repo: pnpm + Nx | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| UI: Tailwind + tokens + Storybook | 5 | 4 | 5 | **3** | **3** | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| Interactive components | **3** | **2** | 4 | **3** | **3** | **3** | **2** | 4 | **3** |
| Data: OpenAPI + Query + Zustand + XState | 4 | 4 | 5 | **3** | 4 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 5 |
| Language/date: i18next + date-fns | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 |
| Testing and quality gates | 4 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 5 | **3** | 5 | 5 |

### Reasons for every score below 4

- **UI: maintenance 3, explicit 3.** Utility-only translation would erase the semantic names such as `.kpi`, `.fresh`, `.save`, `.pipeline`, `.board`, `.canvas`, which now create a direct link to SG-6. With 40 people, reviewers would have to infer the component from a class string instead of reading the contract name. [Observation: `wireframe.css`, SG-6]
- **Interactive components: stable 3, few bugs 2, maintenance 3, explicit 3, scale 3, scales fast 2, mobile 3.** The risk does not lie in React Aria or React Flow individually but in the custom part that connects them to the virtualized treegrid, editor parity, PLT-06 and the responsive card mode. [Observation: WBS-20, BLD-13, PLT-06, SG-5.1/7a]
- **Data: maintenance 3.** OpenAPI has no backend yet but is already treated as the only source; six XState machines also create two parallel kinds of lifecycle model when the domain state already has transition rules. [Observation: section 15.2, section 18.4]
- **Testing: scales fast 3.** 58 screenshot diffs × browsers × viewports plus axe/Storybook/E2E can become a slow and noisy gate; mid-fidelity pixel baselines also make the team spend time handling changes that are correct. [Observation: 58 PNG, appendix B.3]

### Assessment

The stack **has no foundational problem**. The low scores concentrate exactly where Metis has hard domain interaction. So there is no need to replace React/Vite/Nx in order to “refresh the stack”. What is needed is to change how complexity is owned.

# 3. Framework: S2

## 3.1 Is React the best choice for this product?

**Yes, given the current stack and requirements.** It is not only the safest choice. The three hardest widgets of Metis make the integration ecosystem more important than the brevity of component syntax.

### Observation from the attached documents

- `26-wbs-table` is an editable hierarchical table, with pinned columns, bulk actions, saved views, an inline date picker, locks, density and a keyboard grid model. [WBS-04..06, WBS-18..20, SG-7a, WF-26]
- `29-deliverable-builder` and `58-process-framework-editor` are not just diagrams. They have a lane model, parent/child, typed links, lag, routing points, deterministic generation and a parity list editor. [BLD-03..05, BLD-12..16, BR-41, WF-29/WF-58]
- `31-plan-board` needs keyboard move semantics and announcements, not just DnD by pointer. [PLN-05, BR-41, SG-7a, WF-31]
- The agency team is assumed to be about 40 developers. [A-07]

### Industry knowledge

React 19.3 was released in 09/2026; the React Foundation was announced within the Linux Foundation in 2026. Vite 8, Storybook 10.x, React Aria Components, TanStack and React Flow are all actively maintained in 2026. [IND-REACT-2026, IND-VITE-8, IND-STORYBOOK-2026, IND-RAC-2026, IND-TANSTACK-TABLE9, IND-XYFLOW-2026]

## 3.2 Comparison on the three hard widgets and a team of 40

| Framework | Treegrid | Canvas | Board/a11y | Team of 40 | Cost of switching from the current stack | Conclusion for Metis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **React** | TanStack + AG Grid + React Aria ecosystem are strong; custom semantics are still hard | `@xyflow/react` is the direct choice | React Aria has primitives and keyboard/DnD patterns | Lowest staffing and integration risk | None | **Keep** |
| Vue 3 | TanStack has an adapter; AG Grid has Vue; lacks React Aria Components | There are graph options for Vue, but `@xyflow/react` is not kept as it is | Must re-choose the a11y primitives and write adapters | Good, but the current setup would have to be split in two | Medium-large | No benefit large enough to justify switching |
| Angular | AG Grid and Angular CDK are strong; good framework governance | Must change the React Flow stack | CDK supports many primitives, but the current contract would have to be rewritten | Very good for large teams; clear lifecycle policy | Large | Fits only if the architectural decision from the start were Angular, not suitable for switching here |
| Svelte 5 | Has headless/data-grid options but fewer well-trodden enterprise paths for this case | Has a flow ecosystem but not equivalent to the whole React stack | Must replace React Aria; team conventions are less standardized | Compiler UX is good but migration/skills cost is higher | Large | No ROI for Metis |
| SolidJS | Smaller ecosystem for enterprise widgets | Must replace most integrations | Must assemble the primitives by hand | Solid 2.0 is still at RC according to the official source 08/2026 | Very large | Lifecycle risk higher than necessary [IND-SOLID-2] |

Angular has one notable advantage: its support/current/LTS policy is published clearly and Angular 22 is active in 2026. [IND-ANGULAR-SUPPORT] But that advantage does not make up for the fact that Metis has already chosen a group of React libraries that fit the three hard widgets very closely.

## 3.3 What does React need added?

React does not provide application architecture. The stack currently lacks an **official router**. With 58 routes and saved filters/search state, the router must be settled before the first screen. The proposal is to choose a typed router and define route/search-param ownership; `TanStack Router` is the natural candidate with the TanStack family, while React Router is still valid. This is an architectural decision, not a syntax preference. [S9/FS-15]

In addition, React context or Zustand should not be used to replace the domain model. React only renders. Metrics, authz, commands, lifecycle transitions and conflict rules must live outside the component tree.

# 4. Tailwind: S3

## 4.1 Is it worth translating 343 lines of CSS that have been through three rounds of review into utility classes?

**Not worth it if the goal is to delete the semantic CSS. Worth it if the goal is to replace the implementation underneath the semantic components.** This is an important difference.

### Observation from the attached documents

`wireframes/assets/wireframe.css` has 343 lines, about 30 KB. It is not some random “legacy CSS blob”. It contains a vocabulary very close to the SG-6 component table: `.kpi`, `.chip`, `.table`, `.board`, `.canvas`, `.pipeline`, `.save`, `.fresh`, `.src` together with their state variants. The wireframes have been through many rounds of review and the 58 HTML files now use the same vocabulary. [WF-CSS, SG-6]

If translated directly:

```html
<div class="rounded-lg border border-... bg-... px-... py-... text-... ...">
```

then a reviewer no longer sees at once “this is the component `Freshness`, state `stale` per BR-39”. They see only style primitives. That is a loss of traceability, not a loss of CSS functionality.

### Industry knowledge

Tailwind v4 supports `@theme` to generate utilities from design tokens and `@theme inline` to alias existing CSS variables. It also allows custom properties for shadows, for example a composite `box-shadow`. So Tailwind **does not force** Metis to replace `tokens.css`; Tailwind can sit underneath the token layer. [IND-TAILWIND-THEME, IND-TAILWIND-SHADOW]

## 4.2 Proposed styling architecture

Keep three clear layers:

```text
brand/tokens.css                         # source of truth, semantic values
packages/design-system/src/theme.css    # Tailwind @theme aliases + cascade layers
packages/design-system/src/components/  # semantic React components
apps/web/features/...                    # only composes components; utilities limited to local layout
```

Principles:

1. **Tokens remain CSS custom properties.** Do not copy hex/px values into the Tailwind config.
2. **Tailwind only generates utilities for tokens that should be used as primitives.** Do not turn every token into a public utility.
3. **Complex components have a semantic class/data-part.** For example `DataGrid`, `FreshnessBadge`, `SaveState`, `StatusChip`, `BoardColumn`, `CanvasLane`.
4. **Complex geometry may use CSS Modules or `@layer components`.** Sticky grid, z-index planes, pseudo-elements, canvas routing, print/screen-reader helpers do not need to be forced into a utility chain.
5. **Feature code must not recreate a semantic component with utilities.** ESLint/custom lint can forbid using some tokens directly outside the design-system.

## 4.3 A concrete tracing mechanism from SG-6 to code

Create the file `packages/design-system/component-contracts.yaml`:

```yaml
- id: SG6-SAVE-STATE
  styleGuide: "6 / Save state"
  requirements: [PLT-05]
  component: "SaveState"
  source: "src/feedback/SaveState.tsx"
  stories:
    - "Feedback/SaveState/Saving"
    - "Feedback/SaveState/Saved"
    - "Feedback/SaveState/Error"
  tokens:
    - "--good"
    - "--critical"
  tests:
    - "SaveState.interaction.test.tsx"
    - "save-state.spec.ts"
  usedBy: [42-editor-states]
```

The CI gate checks:

- every component row in SG-6 must have an `id`;
- the `component` source exists;
- the story exists;
- the test exists;
- every screen contract that declares a component ID resolves;
- a deprecated component must have a replacement and a migration note.

This is a better mechanism than relying on CSS class names. It keeps traceability even after the styling engine is changed again within 5 years.

## 4.4 Map `tokens.css` into Tailwind

Do not change the original file. Aliases have a prefix to avoid self-reference:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "../../brand/tokens.css";

@theme inline {
  --color-metis-canvas: var(--canvas);
  --color-metis-surface: var(--surface);
  --color-metis-text: var(--text);
  --color-metis-muted: var(--muted);
  --color-metis-violet: var(--violet);
  --font-metis-ui: var(--font-ui);
  --radius-metis-card: var(--radius);
}
```

After that `bg-metis-surface`, `text-metis-text`, `font-metis-ui` are aliases to the existing tokens. [Industry knowledge: IND-TAILWIND-THEME]

### Tokens that should not map 1:1 to utilities

**`--focus-ring`.** This is a two-layer shadow. A Tailwind custom-property shadow can be used, but it is better to let a semantic rule own it:

```css
@layer components {
  .metis-focusable:focus-visible {
    box-shadow: var(--focus-ring);
  }
}
```

Reason: if a call site uses both a different box shadow and the focus shadow, utility ordering can make the focus ring disappear. Focus is an accessibility contract and should not be left for feature developers to assemble themselves. [SG-6, SG-7a] [IND-TAILWIND-SHADOW]

**Seven status groups × three values.** `good`, `waiting`, `serious`, `critical`, `running`, `review`, `neutral`, with each group having dot/text/bg. Do not let call sites combine three independent utilities. Use:

```tsx
<StatusChip tone="critical">Blocked</StatusChip>
```

The component maps all three tokens itself. This prevents the case where the background of `critical` goes with the text of `waiting`. [SG-6]

**Chart series/sequential/diverging tokens.** These are a contract with the chart renderer, not a palette for the feature team to take as it likes. The chart component reads custom properties or a typed token adapter.

**Row height 32/36, shell dimensions, mobile tap target.** These values should live in a component variant/density context. Do not let each screen attach `h-[32px]` and `h-[36px]` scattered around. [SG-5.1]

## 4.5 Is the dense table and canvas markup still readable?

If utility-only: **not readable enough for a team of 40**.

For example, one WBS cell may have to encode sticky, focus, selected, locked, editing, conflict, density, hover, grid border and high-contrast. A long class string would turn the behavior contract into “visual soup”. Similarly a canvas node has a selected state, lane coordinates, baseline/lock, route handles and keyboard focus.

Proposal: keep the call site at the level of:

```tsx
<WbsGrid.Cell
  column="plannedStart"
  state={cellState}
  density={density}
/>
```

instead of the call site owning 20 to 40 utility classes. Tailwind still exists inside `WbsGrid.Cell`.

## 4.6 What does Tailwind not solve for Metis?

Tailwind does **not** solve:

- ARIA `treegrid`, focus roving/active-descendant and screen-reader reading order. [SG-7a]
- row/column virtualization. [WBS-20, section 17.1]
- inline edit transaction, dirty state, PLT-05 save state, PLT-06 conflict resolution.
- DnD keyboard parity of the Board/Canvas. [BR-41, BLD-13]
- graph layout, link routing and lane constraints.
- consistency of fixtures/metrics. [BR-32, BR-39]
- design-system governance when 40 people edit at the same time.
- browser/device performance.
- visual approval and product semantics.

In other words, Tailwind reduces the friction of CSS authoring. It does not reduce domain complexity.

## 4.7 Recommended migration path

Do not “rewrite the CSS and only then build the app”. Follow a strangler migration:

1. Import `tokens.css` as it is.
2. Port the shell and 10 to 15 simple primitive components first.
3. Each semantic class in `wireframe.css`, when it is replaced, must have a `component-contracts.yaml` entry.
4. Simple components move their internals to Tailwind.
5. Grid/canvas/board keep CSS Modules or cascade-layer CSS for geometry if the code is clearer.
6. Delete an old selector only after the new Storybook interaction, visual baseline and a11y tests pass.
7. When the 58 screens are complete, `wireframe.css` is no longer a runtime dependency, but traceability still lives in the contract registry.

**Conclusion S3:** keep Tailwind, but correct the decision from **“Tailwind for the whole app”** to **“Tailwind is the default styling engine inside the semantic design system; complex interaction components may use scoped CSS when it is clearer”**. This is a change of implementation policy, not dropping Tailwind.

# 5. Self-built dense table: S4

## 5.1 Mapping each requirement of `26-wbs-table`

Legend: **Built in** = TanStack provides the model primitive directly; **Configuration + glue** = the primitive exists but Metis must connect it; **Self-written** = the behavior/domain/ARIA lives in Metis; **Not guaranteed** = the library cannot commit to the NFR/acceptance by itself.

| Requirement | TanStack Table/Virtual | Level | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tree of at most 5 levels | Expanding/sub-row model | **Built in + domain guard** | `getSubRows`/expanded state are built in; the 5-level limit and Category at level 1 are domain rules. [WBS-02] |
| Category only at level 1, excluded from the count | Not a concern of the table | **Self-written** | Metrics/aggregation must live in the domain/metrics package. [WBS-18] |
| Inline edit on every column except code/duration | Headless render only | **Self-written** | Cell editor registry, transaction, validation, cancel/commit. [WBS-04] |
| Date picker in a cell | No | **Self-written**, using React Aria | Must manage the focus transfer grid → editor → grid. [WBS-04, SG-7a] |
| Freeze code + name | Column pinning state exists | **Configuration + glue** | CSS sticky/z-index/scroll shadows and SR order are Metis's job. [WBS-20] |
| Horizontal scroll | Browser/layout | **Self-written layout** | Better not to virtualize columns if the number of columns is finite, to reduce a11y complexity. |
| Filter Category/Phase/Type/Status/PIC | Column/global filtering | **Built in** | The UI/filter vocabulary is still Metis's. [WBS-05] |
| Filter a child but keep the parent | `filterFromLeafRows` | **Built in** | TanStack v9 supports leaf-up filtering. [IND-TANSTACK-LEAF-FILTER] |
| Filter applies immediately, no Apply | Controlled filter state | **Built in + debounce policy** | No Apply button needed. |
| Multi-select rows | Row selection | **Built in** | Hierarchy selection semantics must be decided clearly. |
| Bulk Status/PIC/Phase/Priority/Risk | Selection only provides the set | **Self-written command layer** | One command per action + audit/activity. [WBS-06] |
| Delete confirms descendants/dependencies | No | **Self-written** | Domain impact query from the graph/WBS model. [WBS-19] |
| Saved views filters/columns/sort/expanded | Controlled state serializable | **Configuration + self-written persistence** | Schema version for the saved view. [WBS-20] |
| Personal/shared views | No | **Self-written** | Ownership/authz/server contract later. |
| 3 column presets | Visibility/order/pinning state | **Configuration** | A preset is a typed object. |
| Density 36/32px, persist per user | The virtualizer has a fixed estimate | **Configuration + self-written** | Fixed heights actually help the virtualizer. [SG-5.1] |
| Arrow navigation between cells | Not TanStack Table | **Self-written** | Grid focus state. [SG-7a] |
| Enter/F2 edit, Esc cancel | No | **Self-written** | Must handle embedded controls. |
| Space select row | The selection model exists | **Self-written keyboard binding** | Do not let Space scroll the page. |
| Left/right expand/collapse | Expanded state exists | **Self-written keyboard binding** | Only on the hierarchy cell. |
| Column header announced when the cell changes | Markup is the app's | **Self-written ARIA** | The header association must survive sticky/scroll. |
| `aria-level`, `aria-expanded`, relation | Markup is the app's | **Self-written ARIA** | The flattened visible row list must recreate the hierarchy semantics. |
| Sort/filter live announcement + row count | No | **Self-written** | `aria-live` semantic message. [SG-7a] |
| Locked baseline cell opens CR flow | No | **Self-written domain interaction** | Not simply edit-disabled. [BR-04, PLT-06] |
| 2.000 rows, p95 usable ≤2s | The virtualizer helps | **Not guaranteed** | Needs a benchmark harness on target hardware/browser. [section 17.1] |
| <768 table → cards | No | **Self-written alternate renderer** | Use the same row/view model, do not render a shrunken grid. [SG-5.1] |

TanStack v9 describes itself as a headless engine: the library handles state, row processing and typed APIs; the application owns all of the markup, semantics, styles and interactions. That is exactly why it is flexible, and also why Metis must not rate the risk as low just because it has chosen TanStack. [IND-TANSTACK-TABLE9]

## 5.2 Specific technical traps

### 5.2.1 Virtualization + `treegrid`

The virtualizer keeps only part of the rows in the DOM. A screen reader cannot “read” a row that does not exist yet. Metis must set at least `aria-rowcount` on the grid and a correct `aria-rowindex` on the rendered rows. For a tree, it must also provide `aria-level`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize` if the acceptance matrix requires the sibling relationship. [SG-7a]

The bigger trap is focus. If the focused cell is unmounted by the virtualizer during scroll/filter/expand, browser focus falls back to `body` or an unwanted position. A **grid focus controller** independent of the DOM is needed. Two patterns can be used:

- roving `tabIndex=0/-1`, but before changing row it must `scrollToIndex` and wait for the target to mount;
- `aria-activedescendant` on the grid container, but the active descendant must exist in the DOM and editor focus still needs its own mechanism.

Do not choose a pattern by feel. The spike must test NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver with filter, expand, edit and horizontal scroll. [SG-7a]

### 5.2.2 Pinned columns

Do not build the pinned area as three independent left/middle/right grid DOMs if it can be avoided. That approach easily creates duplicated rows/cells in the accessibility tree and makes the screen reader read in the wrong order. Prefer **one semantic row**, with the pinned cells using CSS `position: sticky`, in the same DOM order as the logical columns. [WBS-20, SG-7a]

If split panes must be used, the duplicate part must be removed from the accessibility tree and the keyboard model must have a single logical cell map. The testing cost rises sharply.

### 5.2.3 Inline edit in `treegrid`

A cell has two modes: navigation and edit. When entering edit:

1. the grid controller holds the logical cell coordinate;
2. focus moves into the field/date picker;
3. `Esc` cancels and returns focus to the right cell;
4. `Enter` commits per field policy;
5. a server/save conflict must not make the editor context disappear;
6. the validation/error source must be announced; a toast is not enough for PLT-06. [PLT-05, PLT-06, SG-7a, WF-42]

This is a small state machine at the grid/editor layer; each column should not be left to improvise.

### 5.2.4 Filtering that keeps the ancestor

TanStack v9 has `filterFromLeafRows`, so the requirement “if a child matches, the parent stays visible” **does not need to be written from scratch**. [IND-TANSTACK-LEAF-FILTER] However, Metis must still decide the expanded behavior after a filter: automatically open the ancestors of a match, or keep the row in the result but collapsed. The wireframe/BRD need to be turned into a contract so tests are consistent.

### 5.2.5 Density 32/36px

This is the easy part if the row height is fixed. Each density has one exact virtualizer estimate; changing density must invalidate measurements and keep the logical scroll anchor. Rows should not be auto-height in the WBS without a requirement, because auto-height makes virtualization, sticky focus and scroll restoration harder. [SG-5.1]

### 5.2.6 Sort/filter/expand and stable row identity

WBS-03 has a permanent internal ID. The grid must key by that ID, not by row index or WBS code because the code can be renumbered. If the key is wrong, edit state/selection/focus will “jump” to another item after filter/sort/renumber. [WBS-03]

### 5.2.7 React render cost

2.000 rows are not large for the data model, but complex cell renderers can be large. Avoid subscribing the whole grid to a shared save state/Zustand. Query cache updates need structural sharing; scope edit state by row/cell. The React Profiler and a browser performance trace must be part of the benchmark gate.

## 5.3 [Estimate] Effort of custom TanStack

### Assumptions

- Front-end only. The production backend is not counted.
- The WBS has at most about 12 to 16 visible columns at a time; only rows are virtualized, columns are not virtualized at baseline.
- There is 1 front-end architect, 2 senior FEs focused on the grid, 1 shared QA automation/a11y.
- Use React Aria for inner controls, not as the whole grid engine.
- Acceptance includes Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari desktop and a real SR pass before the pilot.

| Item | Estimated engineer-weeks |
|---|---:|
| Core grid shell, columns, sticky, sort/filter/select/expand | 3 to 5 |
| Hierarchy filtering, saved view, presets, density, scroll/focus restore | 3 to 5 |
| Inline editor registry, date field, bulk command, lock/baseline integration | 4 to 6 |
| Keyboard/ARIA treegrid + live announcements + virtualization focus | 5 to 8 |
| PLT-05/06 save/conflict integration and regression states | 3 to 5 |
| Performance benchmark + browser/SR hardening + mobile card renderer | 4 to 6 |
| **Total FE** | **22 to 35 engineer-weeks** |
| QA/a11y automation + manual matrices | **6 to 10 additional engineer-weeks** |

With 3 to 4 people working in parallel, elapsed time **does not divide linearly** because the focus architecture, DOM semantics and command model are sequential work. [Estimate] A range of **8 to 12 calendar weeks** to reach pilot quality for the WBS is reasonable; adding the flat grids afterwards is cheaper because the engine is reused. This is not a project schedule commitment.

## 5.4 Comparing four options

| Option | Stable | Few bugs | Community | Maintenance | Explicit | Scale | Scales fast | 5 years | Mobile | Main strength/weakness |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **TanStack Table + Virtual + Metis layer** | 4 | 3 | 5 | 4 once mature | 5 | 5 | 3 | 5 | 4 | Maximum control over semantics; pays the price in engineering/a11y |
| **AG Grid Enterprise** | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 5 | **5** | 5 | 3 | Fastest feature coverage; vendor/license/theme/a11y constraints |
| **Glide Data Grid** | 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 3 | **5** | 4 | 4 | 3 | Very fast canvas rendering; the WBS hierarchy/ARIA contract fits less naturally |
| **Fully self-built** | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 5 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 3 | No economic/technical reason to build sorting/filtering/selection/virtualizer ourselves |

### AG Grid Enterprise

AG Grid currently provides keyboard navigation, editing and ARIA `grid/treegrid`; Tree Data creates `role="treegrid"`. [IND-AGGRID-KEYBOARD, IND-AGGRID-A11Y] This is a big advantage in time-to-feature.

But the main AG Grid documentation also states clearly: virtualization and DOM order can cause inconsistent announcements; to optimize accessibility they recommend `ensureDomOrder`, turning off sticky group rows, and, in the strongest configuration, turning off row/column virtualization or using pagination. [IND-AGGRID-A11Y] This can conflict with the scroll experience of the WBS and the goal of 2.000 items. So a real test is needed, not scoring a feature matrix.

The current list price is **from USD 999/developer, perpetual, including one year of updates/support**, with volume discounts. [IND-AGGRID-PRICE] [Estimate] If we assume all 40 front-end JavaScript developers must be licensed and ignore discounts/deployment terms, the nominal multiplication is **USD 39.960**. This is **not a quote**; AG Grid must be asked to confirm licensing for an agency/customer-facing SaaS structure before the decision.

### Glide Data Grid

Glide uses canvas and is optimized for a very large number of cells. It has editing/selection and claims accessibility is first-class, but its tree support leans toward cell/building blocks rather than a DOM `treegrid` with deeply customizable semantics. [IND-GLIDE-2026] With Metis having only 2.000 WBS items, the extreme-scale advantage does not offset the SG-7a acceptance risk. Choose it only if a benchmark proves the DOM grid fails on performance and the accessibility contract is proven separately.

### Self-built without TanStack

No advantage. The team would have to recreate column state, sorting, filtering, selection, expansion, memoization and virtualization plumbing before touching the domain requirements. It reduces vendor dependency but raises the “Metis dependency” onto the custom code itself. It does not fit the criteria of few bugs, easy to maintain and scales fast.

## 5.5 Should the decision to rule out a commercial grid be reconsidered?

**Yes.** Not because AG Grid is certainly better, but because the value of 20 to 30 engineer-weeks and the large accessibility risk are enough to justify a formal bake-off.

Proposed acceptance spike, at most 10 working days of a small squad:

1. Fixture 2.000 WBS items, depth 5, Category level 1.
2. Pinned code/name, 10+ columns horizontal scroll.
3. `filterFromLeafRows` equivalent and auto-preserve ancestor.
4. Inline text/select/date edit; Enter/F2/Esc.
5. Space multi-select; left/right expand.
6. Live sort/filter announcement + result count.
7. Baseline locked cell → fake change-request flow.
8. 32/36px density switch.
9. NVDA + Chrome/Edge; VoiceOver + Safari; at least one Windows SR path.
10. Performance trace on a mid-range laptop and a separate mobile card path.

**Condition to choose AG Grid:** it passes exactly the SG-7a matrix without having to turn off virtualization in a way that breaks the NFR/UX, the theme does not force breaking SG-6, and the license is confirmed to be suitable.  
**Condition to keep TanStack:** AG Grid fails the semantics/UX or the license/vendor constraint is unacceptable, while the TanStack spike proves the focus/ARIA architecture is feasible.

# 6. Canvas: S5

## 6.1 Are `@xyflow/react` + `elkjs` suitable for all four screens?

**The four screens should not be treated as a single kind of canvas.** Share the canonical model and command layer, but separate the renderer/layout strategy.

### Observation from the 7 hard screens

- `27-wbs-tree` is a read-heavy hierarchy/dependency graph. Vertical/horizontal auto-layout is a direct requirement. This is where ELK fits best. [WBS-08, WBS-09, WF-27]
- `29-deliverable-builder` is a lane/time-offset editor. Node position is not entirely free: lane, day offset, duration and a common start date carry domain meaning. [BLD-03/04, WF-29]
- `58-process-framework-editor` is an even harder authoring tool: lane CRUD/reorder, parent, typed connection + lag, route points, selector resolution and a parity matrix. [BLD-13..16, WF-58]
- `11-lifecycle-framework-designer` in the current wireframe is mainly a structured designer: stage list, details, gates/rules/readiness. It **does not need to be forced into a node-edge canvas** just because it sits in the group of hard editors. [GOV-01..06, GOV-19..22, WF-11]

Proposed split:

| Family | Screens | Renderer | Layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hierarchy/dependency viewer | 27 | React Flow | ELK vertical/horizontal; free-position override when WBS-09 applies |
| Lane/process authoring | 29, 58 | React Flow primitives + Metis custom node/edge/lane layer | Domain coordinate system; ELK used only for helper layout if truly needed |
| Structured lifecycle editor | 11 | React Aria/forms/list reorder | Do not use React Flow by default |

If after Discovery `11` gets a new requirement to visualize the graph, a React Flow view can be added. Do not let the renderer decide the domain model.

## 6.2 Is the model “our own graph, canvas/list are two views” right?

**Right direction, but not enough.** The two views should not both edit the raw graph state directly. A **canonical command layer** is needed in between:

```ts
createNode(cmd)
editNode(cmd)
moveNodeToLane(cmd)
reorderNode(cmd)
setParent(cmd)
createLane(cmd)
renameLane(cmd)
reorderLane(cmd)
deleteLane(cmd)
createConnection(cmd)
setConnectionTypeAndLag(cmd)
deleteConnection(cmd)
addRoutePoint(cmd)
moveRoutePoint(cmd)
deleteRoutePoint(cmd)
```

Each command has:

- stable command ID;
- typed payload;
- precondition/permission;
- expected record/version per PLT-06;
- idempotency key;
- domain validation result;
- audit/event metadata;
- UI intent source: canvas, list, keyboard, MCP/API later.

The BLD-13 parity matrix maps **gesture → keyboard → list action → command ID**, not directly to a React handler. [BLD-13, BR-41, PLT-06, section 18.4]

### Another feasible approach

An event-sourced reducer can be used: every UI emits a domain event/intention and a reducer builds the new graph. In essence it is still the same principle: **one operation vocabulary**, many input adapters. So a “shared graph model” is not the only way, but “shared operation semantics” is almost mandatory if BLD-13 and PLT-06 are to be durable.

## 6.3 How far does React Flow's keyboard support go today?

According to the current React Flow documentation, node/edge focusability and some basic keyboard interactions already exist: Tab to focus, Enter/Space to select, Esc to clear, arrow keys to move a selected draggable node, and auto-pan on focus. ARIA labels can be configured. [Industry knowledge: IND-XYFLOW-2026]

But Metis must still write on its own:

- `C` to start a connection per the WF-58 matrix;
- lane-aware up/down and reorder semantics;
- parent assignment (`Alt+P` per the wireframe digest);
- create/rename/reorder/delete lane;
- edge type + lag editor;
- route-point add/move/delete;
- domain-aware live announcements;
- focus traversal by lane order instead of the default DOM/order;
- keyboard/list/server-command parity enforcement;
- validation and recovery when a command is rejected by PLT-06.

React Flow accessibility is a foundation, not an acceptance solution for BLD-13.

## 6.4 Should ELK run on the main thread?

For a small graph it can be fine, but auto-layout can create a long task when the graph is large or when it runs continuously during editing. Proposal: a `layout-engine` adapter with an async boundary; if a benchmark shows a >50ms long task on the target device, then move ELK to a Web Worker. A worker is not mandated from day one; what is mandated is **no component imports ELK directly**, so the path to move always stays open. [WBS-08, section 17.1]

## 6.5 Two people editing the same canvas

The BRD section 20 solution “one person edits one canvas at a time” is **acceptable for the MVP**, if it is a server-enforced lease and not a flag in the browser.

Minimum contract:

- lock owner, acquired-at, expires-at;
- heartbeat/TTL;
- read-only observer mode;
- takeover/request-control flow;
- losing the lock mid-session → stop writing, keep the local unsaved command log and allow copy/recover;
- the lock scope is a specific canvas/version, not locking the whole project;
- PLT-06 version/idempotency still applies. A lock reduces conflicts, it does not replace the conflict contract.

If only a browser/local flag is used, two tabs or two machines still overwrite each other. That contradicts PLT-06.

**Conclusion S5:** keep React Flow. Use ELK for graph auto-layout, do not treat ELK as the lane-authoring engine. It is mandatory to add an `editor-core` containing the canonical commands and parity adapters before coding the editor.

# 7. Data and contracts: S6

## 7.1 Is “one OpenAPI file generates four things” sound?

**It can be sound at the transport layer, but it should not be the only source of the domain.** A modern generator can generate TypeScript types/client, React Query hooks, Zod schemas and MSW handlers. Orval now has official documentation for React Query, Zod and MSW; Kubb also has equivalent plugins. [Industry knowledge: IND-ORVAL-2026, IND-KUBB-2026]

Concrete proposal:

```text
packages/contracts/
  domain/
    commands.ts              # authored, stable semantics
    errors.ts
    metric-snapshot.ts
    write-envelope.ts        # version + idempotency + actor/source
  openapi/
    provisional.yaml         # generated/edited transport contract for prototype
  generated/
    client/                  # Orval output
    schemas/                 # Zod output
    mocks/                   # MSW output
```

Use **Orval** as the default generator because one config can have multiple outputs and the tool already supports React Query + Zod + MSW. Do not let generated code be imported from `packages/domain`. The dependency direction must be domain-independent → transport adapter, not the reverse. [section 18.4]

## 7.2 The risk of the FE thinking up the API before the backend

The real risk is not “the API will later differ by a few endpoints”. The risk is that **the FE unintentionally turns the UI shape into a business contract**:

- one endpoint per screen instead of resource/command semantics;
- DTOs mixed with display-only fields;
- PATCH semantics that do not support expected-version/idempotency;
- metric values recalculated by the FE instead of a snapshot/version from the server;
- permission filtering that happens only client-side;
- a conflict payload without enough `mine/theirs/base` for a PLT-06 merge.

Ways to reduce it:

1. Call the current spec `provisional.yaml`; do not promote it as the final API.
2. Domain command/error/write-envelope are authored separately per PLT-06 and 18.4.
3. The fixture contract must have examples for success, validation, stale version, permission denied, session expired.
4. Generated transport types exist only in `data-access`; features receive the domain/view model through an adapter.
5. The Discovery backend has the right to change the transport without changing command semantics; adapter compile errors show the scope of the migration.
6. Only after the backend contract is settled is the provisional label removed.

## 7.3 Mock Service Worker for tests and demos

**MSW is suitable for unit/integration/E2E mocks and for a single-user front-end demo.** MSW is still actively maintained in 2026. [IND-MSW-2026]

There is no need to build a mock server just to have a screenshot/demo baseline. But three modes must be separated:

- `fixture`: deterministic data, no persistence; for unit/visual.
- `demo`: MSW browser + deterministic persistent scenario store; can be reset to a named scenario.
- `contract-test`: Node/test adapter that simulates write version/idempotency/conflict exactly.

The MSW browser **does not prove** multi-user concurrency, tenant isolation or MCP authorization. Those requirements belong to B.3 and need integration/security evidence later. [TEN-02, MCP-05/07/16/19, appendix B.3]

## 7.4 Are TanStack Query + Zustand enough?

**Enough if the ownership rules are strict.** Proposal:

| State type | Owner |
|---|---|
| Server entities/snapshots | TanStack Query |
| URL route/search/filter shareable | Router |
| Form draft | React Hook Form/local component |
| Grid focus/selection/edit session | Grid controller local/external store of its own |
| Canvas command session | `editor-core`/machine local |
| Small cross-screen UI preference | Zustand |
| Domain lifecycle | pure domain transition table |

Do not copy Query data into Zustand “for ease of use”. That is a source of stale state and merge bugs.

Zustand has regular releases in 2026. [IND-ZUSTAND-2026] It suits small UI stores exactly as the original proposal said.

## 7.5 XState for six state machines

**Reduce from six to two, at most three.** XState is not a bad choice; the problem is using a state machine runtime even for lifecycles that are by nature persistent domain data.

Keep XState for:

1. **Save/conflict orchestration PLT-05/06.** States such as `clean → dirty → saving → saved/error/conflict`, retry, stale-version resolution and the leave-page guard have clear asynchronous behavior.
2. **Onboarding five-step orchestration**, if there is resume/branch/retry/async import that is complex enough. [ONB]
3. **Possibly** use it for a complex editor interaction mode if the spike proves an ordinary reducer becomes ambiguous.

Do not use XState by default for:

- change-request lifecycle;
- tenant lifecycle;
- workspace lifecycle;
- process-framework Draft/Published/Deprecated.

The lifecycles above should be typed transition tables + pure guards in the domain, for example `allowedTransitions[state]`. The server is the authority later. The UI only asks `canTransition`. This avoids the UI machine and the persisted server state becoming two sources of truth.

XState currently has a v6 alpha that is very active in 09/2026 while the stable v5 lineage is still the production foundation. [IND-XSTATE-2026] That is not a red flag, but it is all the more reason not to embed XState deeply in every entity lifecycle during a major-version transition.

# 8. Repo and build tools: S7

## 8.1 Nx vs Turborepo vs pnpm only

**Choose Nx** for Metis.

| Criterion | Nx | Turborepo | pnpm workspaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boundary enforcement | **Strong**, project graph/tags + lint rules | Needs extra ESLint/custom rules | Build it yourself |
| Affected graph/testing | **Strong** | Strong for task/cache | Basic |
| Simplicity | Medium | **High** | **Highest** |
| Explicitness with 40 people | **High if the config is small and the tags are clear** | High but the architecture rules live outside the tool | Low when the repo is large |
| Migration cost if the tool is dropped | Medium | Low-medium | n/a |

The reason for choosing Nx is not a cache that is a few seconds faster. The reason is that A-07 has 40 developers and the most important requirement of the monorepo is **architecture as executable rules**: the domain does not import UI, features do not bypass data-access, the design-system does not import features. Nx has a direct advantage here. [Industry knowledge: IND-NX-2026]

Nx has major releases and a current LTS policy in 2026. [IND-NX-2026]

## 8.2 Do the current five packages have the right boundaries?

Not enough. `packages/domain` will bloat if it contains metrics, roles, state machines and the write contract. `packages/contracts` is also mixing the transport spec with the keyboard/metric matrices, which are not the same runtime concern.

Proposed boundaries:

```text
packages/
  domain/          # core entities, enums, pure business rules, command types
  metrics/         # definitions/version/evaluation/reconciliation fixtures
  authz/           # roles, permissions, generated permission checks
  editor-core/     # graph model, commands, parity IDs, undo/session primitives
  contracts/       # OpenAPI + external schemas + generated contract artifacts
  data-access/     # generated client, Query adapters, MSW handlers
  design-system/   # tokens, semantic components, Storybook
  fixtures/        # named deterministic scenarios, builders
apps/
  web/
```

Do not create a package for each component. A package boundary should exist only when it has its own ownership/import rule.

### Packages that should be split

- `domain` → split out `metrics`, `authz`, `editor-core` because the three areas have different rates of change and different owners.
- `api-client` → rename to `data-access` because besides the generated client there are also Query adapters and the mock boundary.

### Packages that should not exist as runtime packages

The “keyboard equivalence matrices” and “metric definition matrices” are **contract data/test artifacts**. They can live in `contracts/` or `test-contracts/`, but should not make every app bundle import them. Use typed/generated JSON/YAML for tests and Storybook to read; production bundles only the part it really needs.

## 8.3 Where will it get slow first?

In the expected order:

1. **Playwright matrix**: 58 screens × browsers × viewports × screenshots/a11y.
2. **Storybook interaction/a11y tests** when the number of story states grows to a few hundred.
3. **TypeScript checking of generated API/Zod types** if one large barrel re-exports every schema.
4. **Grid/canvas E2E** with async layout/virtualization and screenshot stabilization.
5. Building the web bundle is not the first problem with Vite 8; the test topology will hurt first. [IND-VITE-8, IND-VITEST-5]

Measures:

- Nx affected tests on PRs; full matrix nightly/release.
- Playwright shards by area/browser.
- Do not run the visual pixel diff of the 58 screens on all three browsers on every PR; use a Chromium PR baseline, a cross-browser interaction smoke, and full cross-browser nightly.
- Generated contracts use direct imports, avoid a mega barrel.
- Cache the Storybook build and test artifacts.
- Separate the performance suite from the correctness suite so as not to create a flaky gate.

## 8.4 Dividing the work among 40 people

Do not divide “1 screen per person” right away. Divide by ownership + the workstreams of section 18.2:

| Group | Ownership |
|---|---|
| Front-end platform (4 to 5) | Nx, routing, app shell, auth/session adapters, PWA, error/telemetry hooks |
| Design system + a11y (5 to 6) | SG-6/7a, tokens, Storybook, component contracts, manual SR protocol |
| Grid squad (4) | grid engine, WBS, portfolio registry/change register adapters |
| Editor squad (5) | `editor-core`, React Flow, parity matrix, Builder/process editor |
| Project execution feature squad (6 to 7) | Overview/Charter/Plan/Change/Reports/Focus/Docs |
| Governance/onboarding squad (5 to 6) | lifecycle/gate/templates/workspace/onboarding |
| Portfolio/access squad (5 to 6) | cockpit/registry/control towers/tenant/profile |
| QA automation/perf embedded (cross-cutting) | test harness, fixtures, perf/a11y gates |

Rules to block conflicts:

- CODEOWNERS for `design-system`, `domain`, `metrics`, `authz`, `editor-core`.
- Nx tags: `scope:*`, `type:domain|ui|data|feature|app`.
- A feature does not import another feature; sharing must go through domain/design-system/data-access.
- Only the design-system owner edits the token/component contract after the baseline is locked.
- Only the metrics owner edits formulas; the UI has no metric calculation function of its own.
- Generated folder read-only in review; CI regenerate-and-diff.

# 9. Testing: S8

## 9.1 The current test pyramid

The proposed direction is right but the visual gate is too heavy and lacks a clear **component/interaction contract test** layer between unit and full Playwright.

Proposed ratios by purpose, not by a hard number of tests:

1. **Pure domain/contract tests: the most.** Metrics, permission, commands, transition guards, fixture invariants.
2. **Component interaction tests: many.** React Aria components, grid cells/editors, save/conflict widgets, board card move, stories.
3. **Feature integration with MSW: moderate.** Query/loading/error/permission/session states.
4. **Playwright critical journeys: fewer but deep.** WBS, Builder, gates, onboarding, approvals, auth/access.
5. **Visual regression: selective.** High-fidelity app baselines, not wireframe pixels.
6. **Manual exploratory/SR: mandatory for the six SG-7a patterns.**

## 9.2 Screenshot gate with 58 wireframes

**Drop it as a pixel gate. Keep the wireframes as a conformance reference.**

Replace it with four layers:

### A. Screen contract

Each screen has a machine-readable contract:

```yaml
screen: 26-wbs-table
route: /projects/:projectId/wbs
requirements: [WBS-01, WBS-02, ...]
components: [Shell, ProjectTabs, WbsGrid, FilterBar, SavedViewMenu, BulkBar]
states: [default, filtered, selected, editing, locked, error]
fixtures: [acme-wbs-default]
a11yPatterns: [editable-treegrid, live-region]
viewports: [desktop, tablet]
```

CI checks the route/component/state/test linkage.

### B. Structural conformance

Story/screen tests assert semantic regions, component contract IDs, critical labels/actions and requirement markers. Do not snapshot the whole DOM class list.

### C. Human wireframe review

When a screen first reaches high-fidelity, the reviewer compares it side by side with the PNG/digest and signs off the baseline. A wrong layout/missing component still shows up without forcing the app to match the mid-fi pixel for pixel.

### D. App visual regression

After the sign-off, screenshots **of the app** become the baseline. From then on a pixel diff is meaningful: it detects regressions of new code against the approved UI.

## 9.3 Checking the nine requirements that B.3 says the wireframes cannot prove

| Requirement | Front-end/contract evidence needed |
|---|---|
| TEN-02 | FE test that every permission state leaks no cached tenant data; but the final negative tenant isolation must be an integration/security test. A UI test is not enough. |
| MCP-05 | A contract fixture confirms that the UI/API capability map uses the same permission identifiers; real authorization belongs to server integration. |
| MCP-07 | PLT-06 stale-version fixture: an old expectedVersion is rejected; the UI renders an inline conflict, not toast-only. |
| MCP-13 | Schema contract tests for tool response fields/pagination/contact scope; the FE only checks the adapter/display if there is one. |
| MCP-16 | FE cannot prove fuzz/security. Keep only schema rejection tests; the security suite belongs to integration. |
| MCP-19 | Data-driven matrix by tool class/confirmation mode; the UI approval surface must render the right mode. |
| BLD-13 | Each parity row generates a keyboard + list command test; an E2E canvas smoke for the same command ID. |
| BLD-14 | Unit/contract fixtures for `resolved`, `missing`, `ambiguous`; forbid auto first-match. |
| BLD-16 | Table-driven publish-check tests for each rule, including connection constraint consistency. |

The important point: do not try to “prove server security with front-end tests”. The test report must state the evidence owner clearly to avoid false confidence.

## 9.4 A metric reconciliation test must break when the calculation is wrong

Do not write four screens that all call `calculateHealth()` and then assert that they are equal. If `calculateHealth()` is wrong, all four are wrong together and the test stays green.

The right design:

1. `metrics/definitions` holds the metric ID + version + formula/algorithm implementation.
2. Create small, hand-verifiable **golden fixtures** with deliberate edge cases: Category must be excluded, zero denominator, overdue boundary, as-of cut-off, missing data.
3. Expected values are stored independently, not generated from the production function.
4. The API/MSW returns a **MetricSnapshot** consisting of value, `asOf`, `definitionVersion`, trace/source IDs.
5. Overview, Focus, Board summary and the report adapter only render/transform the snapshot; an architecture lint forbids importing the metric calculator into feature UI.
6. The test of each surface receives the same fixture and asserts the exact value + version + as-of.
7. Add a mutation/canary test: change one input so that only one formula condition changes; the expected value must change. This catches errors like “Category counted by mistake” or a boundary date.

If you want it stronger, use mutation testing for the `metrics` package; this is an enhancement, not a mandatory first gate.

## 9.5 Accessibility: what do machines check, what do people check?

| SG-7a pattern | Machine-checkable | People/SR must check |
|---|---|---|
| Editable grid/treegrid | role/ARIA presence, keyboard sequence, focus target, live region text, contrast | header/row/level announcements, sticky/virtual reading order, edit-mode speech, long navigation |
| Navigation tree | role/treeitem, arrow/Home/End state, expanded attrs | announcement clarity and focus context |
| Board | keyboard Move-to flow, target lists, live message text | SR announcement after a move, cognitive order between columns |
| Canvas | command parity tests, focusable nodes, keyboard command dispatch | discoverability, reading order, spatial operation equivalence |
| Dialog/drawer | focus trap, initial focus, Esc, return focus, aria-modal/name | SR title/context and nested control flow |
| Status/live region | `aria-live` presence/message updates | timing, duplication, whether message interrupts too much |

`axe-core` must run but **does not replace screen-reader testing**. Axe is actively maintained in 2026, but by nature automated rules do not know whether an announcement matches the product expectation or not. [IND-AXE-2026]

Minimum manual matrix before the pilot:

- NVDA + Chrome or Edge on Windows;
- VoiceOver + Safari on macOS;
- mobile light-update screens: VoiceOver iOS or TalkBack Android, at least one path;
- test at 200%/400% zoom, forced colors/high contrast where appropriate;
- keyboard-only without a screen reader to detect focus traps/shortcut conflicts.

## 9.6 Playwright and Storybook

Playwright is releasing regularly and browser versions are pinned through releases. Storybook 10.x continues to be updated in 2026, with a component/a11y testing workflow. Vitest 5 was released in 09/2026 and focuses on performance. [IND-PLAYWRIGHT-2026, IND-STORYBOOK-2026, IND-VITEST-5]

Recommendations:

- Storybook is the gate for design-system states.
- Vitest/browser-component tests for fast interaction loops.
- Playwright does not repeat every story; it only checks end-to-end composition and browser behavior.
- `axe` runs on stories and representative pages; there is no need to run 58×every state×every browser on each PR.

---
# 10. What is missing: S9

This section **does not repeat** the nine points the team already raised itself about visual diff, Tailwind traceability, custom grid, XState, pre-backend OpenAPI, parity matrix, dark mode/icon, fixture consistency and the auth/CSP/bundle/flags/observability/error boundary/PDF/upload scanning infrastructure.

| What is missing | Consequence if ignored | Concrete proposal | When it must be decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Router and route/search-state contract** | 58 screens each manage URL/filter differently; back/forward/share link breaks | Choose a typed router; define route params, search params, blockers, loaders; route IDs must map to the manifest | **Before the first screen** |
| **Browser support matrix** | Unknown which Safari/WebKit/iOS tests are the release gate | Settle browsers + minimum versions + screen reader/browser pairs; map into Playwright projects | **Before the first component** |
| **Canonical keyboard shortcut registry** | `C`, `Delete`, `Alt+...`, browser/OS/SR shortcuts collide with each other | One registry with scope, command ID, fallback UI, discoverability and a conflict test | **Before the first editor/board** |
| **Focus architecture for virtualized widgets** | Each team builds its own grid/canvas, focus is lost when the DOM unmounts | Design doc + reusable focus controller; spike with the grid first | **Before `26-wbs-table`** |
| **Command/undo policy** | Canvas/list/bulk edit have different semantics; unknown whether undo is local or server | Canonical command envelope; the MVP settles explicitly which undo exists and which does not, never left implicit | **Before the first editor** |
| **Date/time semantic model** | `Date`/timezone/as-of/fiscal dates differ between screens; BR-39 reconciliation is wrong | `packages/domain/time`: Instant/date-only/workspace-zone/as-of; UI formatter adapter; forbid direct `new Date()` in features | **Before the first screen with date edit** |
| **Money/decimal model** | Portfolio budget/benefits have rounding drift | Settle minor units or a decimal representation, currency code and formatting; do not use floating point for persisted money semantics | **Before the portfolio/business-case screens** |
| **Chart library and accessible fallback** | Dashboard teams choose different charts; no data table equivalent | Choose one chart renderer through a `Chart` abstraction; each chart has a textual/table equivalent and a token adapter | **Before `14/15/18/19`** |
| **Error taxonomy** | Toast/message inconsistent; retry/permission/conflict mixed together | Typed error categories: validation, authz, session, conflict, transient, fatal; map to a UI pattern | **Before the first screen** |
| **Localization key governance + pseudolocalization** | English/Vietnamese drift; layout breaks when text is long | Namespaced keys by feature/component; pseudolocale CI; no literal user-facing strings lint | **Before the first screen** |
| **Fixture clock/ID determinism** | Screenshots/tests are flaky because of “now”, random UUIDs, sorting | Seeded ID factory + fixed `Clock`; every named scenario declares `asOf` | **Before the visual/test baseline** |
| **Saved-view schema versioning** | After columns/filters change, an old view crashes or is silently wrong | `SavedViewV1` + migration function + unknown-field policy | **Before the WBS/registry saved views** |
| **URL vs saved-view precedence** | A user opens a shared link but a local view overrides it and gives different results | Settle the precedence: explicit route/search > selected saved view > user default > product default | **Before the WBS/registry** |
| **Design-system change governance** | 40 people fork components or a breaking change spreads across 58 screens | Component contract IDs, owner, deprecation, changelog, review rule | **Before the first component** |
| **Dependency upgrade policy** | Several major releases at once cause migration shock | Pin exact major/minor policy, scheduled monthly patch/quarterly minor review, major upgrade RFC, security override | **Before the repo baseline** |
| **SBOM/license policy for OSS dependencies** | Legal/security review comes late, especially for commercial/dual-license packages | Automated dependency/license inventory; denylist/approval workflow | **Before the pilot**, best before the baseline |
| **Source-map/privacy policy** | Production debugging or leaked source/data labels | Private source map upload to error service; no public sourcemap if policy forbids it | **Before the pilot** |
| **High contrast/forced-colors/reduced-motion policy** | Basic WCAG passes but enterprise users lose affordances | Design-system stories for forced colors, reduced motion; animation does not carry the only information | **Before the pilot**, primitives early |
| **Zoom/reflow acceptance** | Desktop dense screens unusable at 200 to 400% zoom | Add acceptance rows per responsive pattern; table may horizontal scroll where WCAG permits | **Before the pilot**, layout primitives early |
| **PWA data retention model** | Service worker/CacheStorage keeps tenant data unintentionally | Static hashed assets only by default; API NetworkOnly; no offline writes; explicit cache purge on logout/tenant switch | **Before turning on the PWA** |
| **Cross-tab coordination** | Two tabs editing/refreshing the token/save state at once cause hard-to-understand conflicts | BroadcastChannel/storage event adapter for auth/session/lock invalidation; PLT-06 remains authority | **Before the pilot** |
| **Performance budgets per route/widget** | The 2s NFR is too coarse, bundle/interaction regressions do not show early | Bundle KB budget, long-task budget, grid interaction benchmark, canvas layout benchmark, CI trend | **Before the first hard screen** |
| **Main-thread worker policy** | ELK/large parse/export block interaction | Async adapter first; move ELK/heavy computation to a worker when the benchmark exceeds the threshold | **Before the canvas pilot** |
| **Accessibility ownership and sign-off** | “axe green” is misread as WCAG done | A11y owner, six-pattern matrix, manual SR sign-off artifact/version | **Before the first component** |
| **Component telemetry event vocabulary** | After the pilot, user pain at save/grid/filter/editor cannot be compared | Stable event names, no sensitive payload, performance marks for key actions | **Before the pilot** |

# 11. Risk of becoming outdated within 5 years: S10

The risk level is assessed for **Metis depending on that technology**, not only the probability that the upstream project disappears. A healthy project that Metis uses too deeply still has a large exit cost.

| Library/tool | 5-year risk | Signs | Exit path if it dies/changes direction | Exit cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **React** | Low | React 19.3 released 09/2026; large ecosystem; React Foundation 2026. [IND-REACT-2026] | Migrate the framework along feature boundaries; keep the domain/data packages framework-free | **Very large** |
| **TypeScript** | Low | De facto standard for typed JS; strong release cadence. [IND-TS-2026] | JavaScript/JSDoc or a successor compiler; the domain types still have design value | **Very large**, but low probability |
| **Vite** | Low | Vite 8 stable 03/2026, Rolldown integration. [IND-VITE-8] | Rspack/Webpack/other bundler; app code has little dependence if the config is isolated | M |
| **vite-plugin-pwa** | Medium | Has a current release v1.3.0, but is a plugin outside Vite core. [IND-VITE-PWA-2026] | Workbox/custom service worker or drop installability; D-19 does not require offline | M |
| **pnpm** | Low | pnpm 11/12 has continuous releases up to 09/2026. [IND-PNPM-2026] | npm/yarn/bun workspace; lockfile/install scripts migration | M |
| **Nx** | Low to medium | Nx 23.x active, has a support/LTS policy. [IND-NX-2026] | Turborepo + pnpm + ESLint boundary rules | M to L |
| **Tailwind CSS** | Low | v4.x active 2026; strong token/theme APIs. [IND-TAILWIND-2026] | CSS Modules/cascade layers; the semantic component layer reduces the blast radius | M if done per S3; L if utilities are scattered across features |
| **Storybook** | Medium | 10.6 09/2026; the project only actively maintains the latest major/minor. [IND-STORYBOOK-2026] | Another component test runner + docs app; stories can be codemodded/ported | M |
| **React Aria Components** | Low to medium | React Spectrum/Aria releases 1.4 to 1.7 in 05 to 09/2026. [IND-RAC-2026] | Metis's semantic wrapper allows switching to native/Ariakit/Radix-like primitives | M if the wrapper is good; L if imported directly in every feature |
| **TanStack Table** | Low to medium | v9 current, active; headless API separates rendering. [IND-TANSTACK-TABLE9] | AG Grid or a Metis table engine; the domain/view model is kept independent | L for the grid engine, M for flat tables |
| **TanStack Virtual** | Medium | TanStack ecosystem active; narrow primitive but the focus integration is Metis code. [IND-TANSTACK-2026] | React Aria Virtualizer/other virtualizer/custom fixed-row virtualizer | M |
| **TanStack Query** | Low | Large ecosystem, the server-state API model has matured. [IND-TANSTACK-2026] | SWR/custom query cache; isolate in data-access | M |
| **@xyflow/react** | Low to medium | React Flow 12.x has releases and current a11y docs 2026. [IND-XYFLOW-2026] | Canvas adapter to another renderer/custom SVG; the canonical editor-core protects the domain | L |
| **elkjs** | Medium | Has release 0.12.0 and activity in 2026; a specialized project, its implementation lineage is more complex than mainstream UI libs. [IND-ELK-2026] | Dagre/other graph layout/custom layered layout behind the `layout-engine` adapter | M |
| **react-hook-form** | Low | 7.89 released 26/09/2026; v8 beta is also active. [IND-RHF-2026] | Native controlled/uncontrolled form layer or another library; wrapper form fields | M |
| **zod** | Low | Zod 4.x active in 2026. [IND-ZOD-2026] | JSON Schema/Ajv/Valibot-like schema layer; isolate generated validators | M |
| **zustand** | Low | v5.0.x regular releases up to 08/2026. [IND-ZUSTAND-2026] | React external store/useReducer/context; the stores are small so exit is cheap | S to M |
| **xstate** | Medium | v5 stable lineage; v6 is in alpha and very active 09/2026. [IND-XSTATE-2026] | Pure transition tables/reducers; reduce the footprint per S6 | M if 2 machines; L if 6+ machines |
| **i18next** | Low to medium | Long-standing ecosystem; **[Needs verification]** the exact 2026 release cadence was not settled in this lookup | FormatJS/Intl + custom catalog; keep keys framework-neutral | M |
| **react-i18next** | Low to medium | Depends on React+i18next; **[Needs verification]** the exact 2026 release cadence | The app's `t()` adapter/provider; change the binding layer | S to M |
| **date-fns** | Low to medium | v4.4 latest, v5 alpha 05/2026. [IND-DATEFNS-2026] | Native Temporal + Intl; a time adapter is mandatory for a cheap exit | M |
| **OpenAPI** | Low | Open standard, backend-neutral | JSON Schema/other IDL; domain commands do not depend on the generator | M |
| **Orval** *(proposed)* | Medium | v8/docs currently support React Query, Zod, MSW. [IND-ORVAL-2026] | OpenAPI Generator/Kubb/custom fetch generator; generated output is not authored source code | S to M |
| **Mock Service Worker** | Low to medium | 2.14.x has releases 04 to 05/2026. [IND-MSW-2026] | Fetch adapter/local test server; handlers generated from contracts | M |
| **Vitest** | Low | Vitest 5 released 03/09/2026; Vite-aligned. [IND-VITEST-5] | Jest/Node test runner; pure tests have little dependence | M |
| **Playwright** | Low | Release notes are current, browser matrix updated. [IND-PLAYWRIGHT-2026] | WebDriver/Cypress; page-object/test contracts keep the logic | L |
| **axe-core** | Low | 4.13 released 08/2026, updated for web standards. [IND-AXE-2026] | Other Deque tooling/Accessibility Insights/manual rules; axe API usage is small | S to M |
| **ESLint** | Low | ESLint 10.12 released 02/10/2026. [IND-ESLINT-2026] | Oxlint/Biome/custom AST rules; the architecture rules need porting | M |
| **Prettier** | Low | Prettier 3.9 released 27/06/2026. [IND-PRETTIER-2026] | Biome/other formatter; almost no runtime impact | S |

### Points worth noting

1. **Exit cost matters more than “will the project die”.** React is almost certainly healthier than `elkjs`, but if React disappeared the cost of switching would be far larger. Therefore keeping domain/metrics/authz/editor-core framework-free is the most important hedge.
2. **XState is not risky because the project is weak.** The risk is that Metis uses it too widely exactly when upstream is developing a new major. Reducing to 2 machines makes the exit cost noticeably smaller.
3. **Tailwind is easy to exit only if the semantic layer exists.** If the 58 screens own utilities directly, the replacement cost rises sharply.
4. **React Flow is safe only if the graph operations belong to `editor-core`, not to the React Flow node state.**

# 12. The process of generating the 58 screens: S11

## 12.1 Is the process “each screen = one contract from the manifest” enough?

**Not enough yet.** `manifest.json` is currently very good at answering “which screen, which area, which phase, which requirement”, but not enough for two people or two agents to produce the same architecture. If the contract has only route + requirement + digest + fixture + tests, they can still choose different components, different state ownership, different error behavior and a different keyboard model.

The right process should be:

```text
BRD/style guide
    ↓
Screen contract
    ↓
Component-contract resolution
    ↓
Fixture/scenario binding
    ↓
Route + feature implementation
    ↓
Generated checks
    ↓
Human conformance review
    ↓
Approved app visual baseline
```

## 12.2 Generate by area, by 1A/1B, or by component dependency?

**By dependency first, with milestone 1A/1B as a constraint, and area only as ownership.**

- If going purely by area, the Access team could finish 13 screens while the grid/editor primitives are not yet proven.
- If going purely by 1A/1B and ignoring dependency, many screens at the same time will each create their own version of modal/status/table/filter.
- If going purely by component reuse and ignoring milestones, the design system can be optimized but there is no walking skeleton following the real business flow.

Therefore use the six waves below. Many squads can run in parallel **after the shared dependency of the wave has passed**.

## 12.3 The concrete order of the 58 screens

### Wave 1: forcing out the shell, feedback, responsive read surfaces and approval primitives

| Order | Screen | Why it is done here |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `01-sign-in` | Route/auth shell, form primitives, branded unauthenticated layout |
| 2 | `43-access-states` | PLT-04 sets the no-permission/read-only/session-expired standard before the feature forms |
| 3 | `42-editor-states` | PLT-05/06 force the save/conflict/error contract before every editor |
| 4 | `24-project-overview` | KPI/cards/freshness/metrics/as-of + project shell, less interaction than the WBS |
| 5 | `34-focus` | Responsive one-column/light-update surface, proves the <768 policy early |
| 6 | `38-my-approvals` | Approval list/action/dialog, keyboard and permission state; mobile-eligible |

**Exit Wave 1:** the app shell, router, tokens, core buttons/fields/dialog/drawer/status/freshness/save/conflict/permission components, responsive primitives and Storybook contracts are working.

### Wave 2, Milestone 1A: governed project execution

| Order | Screen | Dependency/component forced out |
|---:|---|---|
| 7 | `36-workspace-setup` | Workspace wizard/form foundation |
| 8 | `09-workspace-fields-options` | Settings tables/options/editor primitives |
| 9 | `10-workspace-team-roles` | Role/permission matrix UI |
| 10 | `11-lifecycle-framework-designer` | Governance designer, reorder/list/form, publish readiness |
| 11 | `12-gate-review` | Gate decisions, evidence, BR-42 eligibility |
| 12 | `37-project-create` | Project creation using published lifecycle/template contracts |
| 13 | `25-project-charter` | Long form, autosave/dirty/error/access patterns |
| 14 | `26-wbs-table` | **Hard gate:** reusable dense grid engine/treegrid |
| 15 | `28-wbs-item` | Full item form/activity/dependency state around WBS model |

**Exit Wave 2:** the 1A workflow can be walked from workspace governance → project → WBS/plan → change/gate/report, and the hardest primitives have a clear owner.

### Wave 3: Access, tenant and provider surfaces

These screens can run partly in parallel with Wave 2 after PLT-04, the shell, the settings tables and the authz contracts of Wave 1 are stable.

The reason `14-executive-cockpit` is not done first even though it is important: the cockpit easily creates a “beautiful dashboard stack” that is under no pressure from the WBS/editor. Doing it after the hard primitives helps the dashboard reuse real components instead of defining a hypothetical design system.

Onboarding should use the real components and domain contracts of the product, and not create a separate mini-app.

The V2/V3 screens must be labeled **Planned** per the documents, not rendered as disabled controls. [Observation: manifest + SG-6]

## 12.4 Screens that must be done early because they force out the most reusable components

If we choose only the eight screens with the highest “design-system forcing power”:

1. `42-editor-states`: save/error/conflict.
2. `43-access-states`: permissions/session/read-only.
3. `24-project-overview`: KPI/freshness/cards/project shell.
4. `26-wbs-table`: grid, filters, saved views, cell editors.
5. `31-plan-board`: DnD keyboard/list responsiveness.
6. `11-lifecycle-framework-designer`: structured enterprise editor + readiness/publish.
7. `29-deliverable-builder`: lane/canvas/list parity.
8. `58-process-framework-editor`: command vocabulary and the hardest parity matrix.

This does not mean dropping the other screens. It means not letting 20 people start 20 screens before the eight forcing surfaces produce the shared contracts.

## 12.5 What needs to be added to a screen contract so that a newcomer/agent gets it right the first time?

Each screen contract needs at least:

```yaml
id: 26-wbs-table
route: /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects/:projectId/wbs
phase: MVP
milestone: 1A
area: Project execution
requirements: [...]
businessRules: [BR-04, BR-24]
sourceFiles:
  wireframeHtml: ...
  wireframePng: ...
  digestAnchor: ...

components:
  required: [SG6-FILTER-BAR, SG6-SAVE-STATE, WBS-GRID, ...]
  forbiddenPatterns: [raw-status-color, feature-local-dialog]

data:
  scenario: acme-wbs-default
  asOf: 2026-...
  metricVersion: ...
  sourceOfTruth: ...

states:
  - default
  - filtered
  - multiSelected
  - editing
  - lockedBaseline
  - saveError
  - conflict
  - readOnly
  - noPermission
  - sessionExpired

commands:
  - WBS.UPDATE_FIELD
  - WBS.BULK_UPDATE
  - WBS.DELETE

a11y:
  patterns: [editable-treegrid, live-region]
  matrixRows: [...]
  manualScreenReader: true

responsive:
  desktop: full-grid
  tablet: pinned-two-columns-scroll
  mobile: not-in-D19 | card-list

performance:
  fixtureSize: 2000
  interactionBudget: ...

tests:
  unit: [...]
  component: [...]
  e2e: [...]
  visual: app-baseline-after-approval

telemetry:
  events: [...]

owner: project-execution-grid
reviewers: [design-system, accessibility]
```

Three more principles:

- **The contract does not copy the BRD prose verbatim.** It points to requirement IDs and only adds implementation acceptance data.
- **An agent must not create a new component if an equivalent contract ID already exists.** If one is missing, the agent opens a design-system change first.
- **The build coverage gate does not only check “the requirement has a screen”.** It checks requirement → screen → component/state/test evidence. A requirement that has a screen but no test/state is still not covered.
