# 13. Conclusion and FS table: S12

## 13.1 Final conclusion

# **Can be settled with conditions**

There is no need to replace React, Vite, TypeScript, pnpm or Nx. There is no need to go back to a static prototype. There is no need to wait for the backend. The stack is modern enough and has a good 5-year survival path if the domain/framework boundary is kept as proposed.

What must be corrected is **how complexity is locked down**:

- Tailwind must not become the public styling API of the 58 screens; the semantic design system is the API.
- A dense grid must not be considered “solved” just because TanStack Table + Virtual are combined; there must be an acceptance spike and the commercial-grid option must be reopened.
- Canvas/list must not be coded before the parity/command contract.
- The current OpenAPI is a provisional transport contract, not the business source of truth.
- XState is used only for real orchestration, not to duplicate every persisted lifecycle.
- Visual regression must take the approved high-fidelity app as the baseline, not the mid-fi PNGs as the pixel oracle.

## 13.2 The FS conditions table

| Code | Subject | Problem | Evidence | Concrete proposal | Priority | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FS-01** | Dense grid strategy | Ruling out AG Grid permanently is too early; the custom treegrid carries the biggest risk | WBS-04..06/18..20, SG-7a, section 17.1, WF-26; IND-AGGRID-A11Y | Run a 10-day acceptance spike TanStack vs AG Grid with a fixture of 2.000 rows + real SR; choose after the evidence | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-02** | Grid accessibility architecture | There is no focus/ARIA model yet for the virtualized treegrid + pinned columns | SG-7a, WBS-20 | Settle the one-semantic-row DOM, focus controller, aria-rowindex/level/expanded, edit-mode protocol; document before the grid build | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-03** | Tailwind/design system | Utility-only loses SG-6 traceability and makes the grid/canvas markup hard to review | SG-6, `wireframe.css`, `tokens.css` | Tailwind under semantic React components; `component-contracts.yaml`; allow scoped CSS for complex geometry | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-04** | Token integration | Composite/status tokens are easily mapped wrongly into loose utilities | `tokens.css`, SG-6/7a | `@theme inline` only aliases safe primitives; focus/status/chart tokens stay in a semantic adapter/component | Should fix in Discovery | S |
| **FS-05** | BLD-13 parity | The matrix does not exist yet but tests/editor depend on it | BLD-13, BR-41, section 18.4, WF-58 | Author the parity matrix before production editor code; each row has a stable operation ID | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-06** | Editor core | Canvas/list easily form two behavior implementations | BLD-03/04/13, PLT-06 | Create `editor-core`: graph model + canonical commands + validators + adapters; the UI does not mutate the raw graph | **Must fix before writing the spec** | L |
| **FS-07** | Canvas layout | Using ELK for every canvas would get the domain lane/time semantics wrong | WBS-08/09, BLD-03, WF-27/29/58 | ELK for hierarchy auto-layout; the lane editor uses domain coordinates; async layout adapter | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-08** | Lifecycle designer | Risk of forcing screen 11 into React Flow just to unify the stack | WF-11, GOV requirements | Keep the structured list/form editor; only add a graph view if a new requirement proves it is needed | Should fix in Discovery | S |
| **FS-09** | API contract | OpenAPI before the backend can lock in a UI-shaped API | PLT-06, section 18.4 | Separate the authored domain commands/errors/write envelope from `provisional.yaml`; generated code only in data-access | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-10** | Code generation | “One file generates four things” lacks clear tool/config ownership | S6 | Use an Orval config with named outputs for client/Query/Zod/MSW; regenerate-and-diff CI | Should fix in Discovery | S |
| **FS-11** | Mock architecture | An MSW demo is easily misread as proof of concurrency/security | B.3, TEN-02, MCP-05/07/16/19 | Separate the fixture/demo/contract-test modes; state the evidence owner clearly | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-12** | State machines | 6 XState machines create duplicate lifecycle models | section 15.2 | Keep XState for save/conflict + onboarding; persistent lifecycles are pure typed transition tables | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-13** | Repo boundaries | `domain` and `contracts` will bloat | repo proposal + section 18.4 | Split out `metrics`, `authz`, `editor-core`, `data-access`; Nx tags/enforce boundaries | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-14** | Router | The 58 routes have no routing/state contract yet | manifest 58 screens | Choose a typed router; route IDs map to the manifest; unified URL/search ownership and blockers | **Must fix before writing the spec** | S |
| **FS-15** | Visual regression | A mid-fi PNG pixel gate causes false positives | 58 PNG, SG-6 | Screen/structure contract + human conformance; app-approved baseline for future pixel diffs | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-16** | Requirement coverage | “The requirement has a screen” does not prove the state/test was done | manifest + B.3 | Coverage graph requirement → screen → state → component → test/evidence; the build fails when the chain is missing | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-17** | Metrics | A cross-screen equality test can be green even when the shared formula is wrong | BR-32/39, OVW-01, section 12 | Independent golden fixtures + MetricSnapshot; forbid screen-local calculation | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-18** | Fixtures | The 58 screens easily drift from the counts/amounts in the BRD | BLD-05; for example CGI 16/15, Nova Energy figures | Named scenario builders + invariants + fixed clock/IDs + fixture contract tests | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-19** | Accessibility QA | axe does not prove the keyboard/SR matrices | SG-7a, BLD-13 | Data-driven keyboard tests + real NVDA/VoiceOver sign-off artifact before pilot | Should fix in Discovery | L |
| **FS-20** | Browser/device target | “Every device” has no concrete test matrix yet | SG-5.1, D-19, section 17.1 | Settle the browser/version/SR pairs and target mid-range devices; Playwright project matrix | Should fix in Discovery | S |
| **FS-21** | Performance | The 2s p95 has no reproducible frontend benchmark | section 17.1 | 2k-WBS scenario, interaction marks, bundle/long-task budgets, trend CI; ELK worker threshold | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-22** | PWA | An installable web app risks caching tenant/auth data and a stale app | D-19 + stack proposal | Precache static assets only; API NetworkOnly; no offline writes; logout/tenant-switch cache purge | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-23** | Date/time/money | The library choice exists but the semantic model does not | BR-39, metric as-of, portfolio money | Domain time/currency adapters; no raw date/float-money logic in screens | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-24** | Screen generation | The manifest contract is not enough to stop 40 people/agents from diverging | manifest, 58 screens | Add component IDs, states, commands, a11y rows, fixture, perf, responsive, owner, tests as in S11 | **Must fix before writing the spec** | M |
| **FS-25** | Design-system governance | Components can fork per feature | SG-6 + 40-person assumption | CODEOWNERS + deprecation/change policy + Storybook contract ID; feature cannot recreate semantic component | **Must fix before writing the spec** | S |
| **FS-26** | Keyboard shortcuts | Canvas/board shortcuts can collide with OS/browser/SR | SG-7a, BR-41, WF-58 | Global shortcut registry, scope/fallback menu/help, automated collision test | Should fix in Discovery | S |
| **FS-27** | High contrast/zoom | The WCAG target has no clear forced-colors/zoom acceptance yet | D-26, SG-7a | Storybook states + 200/400% zoom + forced-colors/reduced-motion checks | Should fix in Discovery | M |
| **FS-28** | Dependency lifecycle | A 5-year target but no upgrade policy yet | S10 | Monthly security/patch, scheduled minors, RFC for majors; pin reproducible toolchain | May be considered | S |

## 13.3 Three decisions to settle before the first line of production code

1. **Grid strategy acceptance contract**: the license need not be signed before the spike, but it must be settled that the production grid is chosen only after the FS-01/02 spike and must pass SG-7a + NFR. Discovery spike code must not be treated as the production implementation.
2. **Semantic design-system contract on top of Tailwind**: component registry, token mapping, ownership and the rule “features do not recreate semantic components”.
3. **Canonical editor operation model**: parity matrix schema + command IDs + `editor-core` boundary for canvas/list/keyboard/write contract.

Three decisions that can be left for later:

1. **The specific icon pack.** Before the high-fidelity visual freeze is enough if from the start there is an `Icon` component and a 1.5px stroke rule. [SG-9]
2. **The dark mode visual palette.** Can come after the pilot; tokens must be semantic from the start so as not to lock light colors into components. [SG-9]
3. **The date to move to Temporal.** Keep `date-fns` behind the time adapter; move when the browser/support policy fits, and do not let features import the time API directly.

## 13.4 The two most contentious decisions

### Tailwind

**Not wrong.** Wrong only if the decision is understood as “all styling must appear as utility classes in the feature markup”. With the hybrid policy in S3, Tailwind meets the goals of community, speed, responsiveness and lifecycle without breaking traceability.

There is no need to go back to CSS Modules entirely. CSS Modules is only a deliberate escape hatch for grid/canvas/complex geometry. This is a third option, better than the binary debate of Tailwind vs CSS Modules.

### Self-built dense table

**The decision “do not buy a commercial grid in any case” lacks sufficient evidence and should be changed into a conditional decision.**

- [Estimate] Custom TanStack WBS at pilot quality: **22 to 35 FE engineer-weeks + 6 to 10 QA/a11y engineer-weeks**, about **8 to 12 calendar weeks** with a dedicated squad and limited parallel work.
- AG Grid current list price: **from USD 999/developer**. [IND-AGGRID-PRICE]
- [Arithmetic estimate, not a quote] 40 × 999 = **USD 39.960** before volume discount and before confirming the licensing/deployment terms.
- AG Grid still has an accessibility trade-off with virtualization; the docs themselves call for mitigations that can affect performance/scroll. [IND-AGGRID-A11Y]

So “AG Grid wins” cannot be concluded from the amount of money. But it is also unreasonable to refuse to test an option that could buy back dozens of engineer-weeks. **FS-01 is a mandatory condition.**

- Main BRD: the parts/codes the prompt asked for, including section 12, 17/17.1, 18.2/18.3/18.4, WBS, BLD, PLN-05, OVW, PLT-04..06, BR-22..24/32/39..42, appendix B.3.
- BRD onboarding/addendum to the extent needed to check the manifest/onboarding order.

### Visual observation from the 7 hard screens

- `26-wbs-table`: high density, hierarchy indentation, many columns, filter/saved views/presets, bulk-selection bar, focus/lock states.
- `58-process-framework-editor`: one screen that holds at the same time a lane canvas, node template/editor, connection editor, parity matrix, selector outcomes and the list equivalent. This is the strongest evidence for needing `editor-core`.
- `29-deliverable-builder`: wizard/form + swimlane editor + preview/list; the sample quantity of CGI Still Renders, 16 items/15 relationships, must be turned into a fixture invariant.
- `42-editor-states`: save failure + inline conflict compare/merge + stale versions + unsaved exit.
- `31-plan-board`: the keyboard “Move to…” flow is clearly shown on the wireframe.
- `27-wbs-tree`: hierarchy/dependencies + auto layout + conflict/incomplete links.
- `11-lifecycle-framework-designer`: structured stage/gate/rule editor; there is currently no reason to force it into a graph canvas.

## 14.2 Assumptions used for the estimate

1. A high-fidelity front-end prototype with sample data, no production backend yet, as the prompt premise states.
2. The agency has about 40 developers but not all 40 work on the grid/canvas.
3. The WBS grid baseline has row-virtualization only; the number of visible columns is small enough that column virtualization is not needed. If a requirement later needs dozens/hundreds of dynamic columns, the estimate must be redone.
4. The accessibility target is WCAG 2.2 AA with a manual SR pass before the pilot.
5. The performance benchmark must be measured on the target browser/hardware settled by Discovery; do not use a high-end dev machine as the only standard.
6. The estimate does not include the backend, production infra, security penetration test or MCP server implementation.

## 14.3 List of `[Needs verification]`

- **The actual AG Grid licensing for an agency + customer-facing multi-tenant SaaS.** USD 999/developer is the list price on the review date; the number of developers to buy, the deployment terms and the volume discount need to be confirmed in writing with the vendor.
- **Target-device performance.** There is no real p95 figure for Metis before an executable spike exists; every performance estimate in the report is an architecture/effort estimate, not a benchmark result.
- **The final screen-reader/browser support matrix.** SG-7a requires a real SR pass but which NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver/TalkBack combination is the release gate needs Discovery to settle with the customer population.
- **The exact i18next/react-i18next release cadence in 2026.** The library is regarded as mature but this lookup did not lock a specific release source; the lifecycle rating is therefore recorded as low to medium instead of absolutely low.
- **Future dark-mode scope.** The style guide says it is not designed yet; the report only ensures the architecture does not block dark mode, and does not assume dark mode will be a requirement.
- **The exact production CSP/auth-token/feature-flag/telemetry vendors.** These are infrastructure decisions the team itself admitted are missing; there is no vendor choice in the pack so the report does not invent one.
